primary_findings: The remand branch works: all four intentionally malformed resident bodies were routed to remand_required.
The harness did not silently repair polluted fixed fields, nearest-class repair, malformed row objects, or bad competency claim status.
Negative-control prompting produced extra row-shape violations beyond the targeted errors, which is useful because the remand circuit preserves the complete error set.
Together with probe 011, this establishes a two-outcome local circuit: accepted_filing for valid assembled artifacts and remand_required for malformed or semantically unsafe filings.
recommended_next_iteration: Add a real remand-response round: give the model the remand filing and ask it to produce a corrected body.
Track whether correction preserves the original semantic route or overcorrects by changing intent.
Add a transition artifact that records declaration_body_submitted -> remand_required -> corrected_body_submitted -> accepted_filing.
Keep automatic repair forbidden; the model must resubmit a corrected body and the harness must validate it.
overall_assessment: Probe 012 validates the fail-closed half of the meta-loop circuit. The harness can reject malformed or semantically unsafe resident filings and record explicit remand reasons without pretending the filing was accepted.
